newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel slams Arab League decision.
newsitem.headline: Israel slams Arab League decision.

text.p: Israel branded as absurd an Arab League resolution on Sunday recommending that member countries suspend steps towards normal relations with it.
"Normal neighbourly relations and regional co-operation are supposed to be an asset and a common interest for all countries in this region," Foreign Ministry spokesman Ygal Palmor told Reuters.
"It is absurd that they are being deemed as a whip, so to speak, to be used against Israel whenever there is a crisis in the peace process," he said.

In Cairo, Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara and Palestinian leader Farouk Kaddoumi told reporters that the same resolution, which passed unanimously, also recommended restoring the Arab boycott of Israel.
The decision was taken at the regular six-monthly meeting of foreign ministers of Arab League states at the league headquarters in Cairo.
It was the latest blow to the Middle East peace process which was plunged into crisis this month when Israel broke ground for a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Palestinians say settlement in Jerusalem pre-empts negotiations which are to be held on the city's status at final peace talks. Palestinian youths have clashed with Israeli troops for 11 straight days in unrest spurred by the settlement.

The final text was not immediately available but a draft in circulation earlier recommended Arab states stop normalisation, reactivate the boycott, close down Israeli offices and missions and withdraw from multilateral Middle East talks.
Shara, asked if the boycott was in the text, said: "Yes, yes, clearly... It is clearer and stronger and it has been adopted unanimously."

Kaddoumi said: "They (the ministers) have emphasised their boycott at the first degree." The first-degree boycott, abandoned by same Arab states over the past three years, bans direct commercial dealings with Israeli companies.
